slides.notes:
WHAT WE DID: index of the May asks (G1-G5, notes/thesis_update_briefing.md §3-4) against what landed.
G1 direct weight inversion: theta_T = F(theta_0, x_hat) with autograd through an unrolled SGD; recovers digits at
N=4 (ssim_norm ~0.57, job 500913) and superposes at N=10 (0.27) and N=20 (~0.15, job 887704). SimuDy (Tian et al.
ICLR 2025, sent by Gal 2026-06-29) publishes the same primitive for full FT -> we reframed onto LoRA-only leakage,
identifiability theory, linearized (memory-tractable) inversion (STATUS.md 'SimuDy collision', notes/simudy_decision_brief.md).
G2 more data: full-gradient ceiling recognizable on MNIST / Fashion / CIFAR-10 / Flowers (SSIM up to ~0.99) and
ViT-B/16 faces; the adapter-only pixel inversion is the open extraction milestone (E7 in thesis_note_v2.md).
G3 smooth activations (his top ask; his prediction: smoother -> NTK survives -> leaks more): the free-coefficient
weight-change ladder shows the opposite on MNIST - kinked cluster ~5x the smooth cluster (job 392821).
G4 midpoint anchor: two-curve plot done (job 532232, MNIST; flowers replicate). Linearization error falls with alpha;
leakage on the realistic control-margin metric does not track it (relu flat; softplus best at alpha=0).
G5 mechanism: the activation enters the whole theory only through sigma' (gate matrix M). Informativeness = rank of
the static M (kink wins); linearization fidelity = continuity of dM (smooth wins). Two objects, opposite directions.
L-BFGS (OUR OWN robustness check, NOT a May ask — removed from the table; mention only if the optimizer question comes up): implemented for the NTK least-squares (LESSONS_LEARNED.md 'L-BFGS vs SGD', 2026-02-22). Full model: L-BFGS
stalls in a shallow basin (SSIM ~0.82 vs SGD 0.996). LoRA r=8: both optimizers hit the same plateau (rank-mismatch
residual) -> the optimizer is not the bottleneck. The validated free-c recipe is SGD extraction + near-ReLU surrogate +
consistency + restarts (STATUS.md 'REALISTIC free-coefficient results'); L-BFGS is kept for quick rank sweeps.
THE INSTRUMENT (say the origin openly): the whitened secret-swap sensitivity d^2 / q_eff (Parts 2-4) - an attack-independent read of how many
private directions the adapter records above its own seed noise. IDEA PROVENANCE: the J_SNR / q_eff construction and the controlled-coordinate experiment design were sparked in an AI working session; the estimators, nulls, gates, and all experiments are ours.
CAVEATS: all Part-1 numbers are MNIST toy MLP unless stated; N=2, T=1 or T=10, rank 8; small n. Observe, don't conclude.

runs.text: with free coefficients and matched weight change, kinked activations leak about 5× more than smooth ones
similarity to the private image minus similarity to a same-class control — cancels the shared background

red = kinked, green = smooth; diamonds = oracle coefficients (upper bound).  T = 1 is the only regime where ‖ΔW‖ can be matched exactly across the 13 activations; the T-sweep and the T=1000 battery carry the realistic one
every number here is an explicit-attack reconstruction — a lower bound on real leakage (prior-free, adapter-only, per-image)
standard methods used here: SSIM (structural similarity) for the reconstruction score

slides.notes:
WHAT WE DID: MNIST, N=2, T=1, LoRA rank 8, 13 activations, realistic FREE-coefficient attack (Haim-style;
oracle = diamonds, upper bound only). Four matched weight-change rungs {0.005, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3}; the bars show one rung
(0.1). Leakage = ctrl_margin_norm (experiments/recompute_metrics.py:87): ssim_norm(recon, private) minus
ssim_norm(recon, same-class control), mean/std-matched SSIM.
CLAIM+HOW (one breath): at equal weight change, kinked activations leak ~5x more than smooth — same free-c attack, 13 activations, control-margin metric; the bars are one matched rung, the ordering holds at all four. WHY T=1 (if asked): matched weight change is what makes 13 activations comparable, and it is exact only for one step (one step = the raw gradient rescaled to the rung; more steps entangle lr and trajectory, so the rungs stop being matched). STATUS marks the T=1 ladder first-pass. The realistic-T side of the deck: slide 4 sweeps T to 50, the anchor runs T=10 (relu-vs-softplus ordering consistent), the whole part-4 battery is T=1000. WHY THIS FUNCTION: the control margin is the instance-leakage bar - it cancels the shared background/clipping that makes
absolute SSIM untrustworthy at small N, and it is clip-robust (not raw ctrl_margin, not eff_rank).
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: the two-cluster gap (kinked mean ~0.47 vs smooth mean ~0.09) holds at EVERY rung; Spearman(smoothness,
leakage) is negative at every rung (-0.48 / -0.25 / -0.27 / -0.59) and strengthens with weight change. Oracle tracks free-c
closely, so the ordering is robust to both attack mode and weight change. Do NOT quote a single canonical Spearman: the
exact value depends on the smoothness ORDERING (no unique total order over 13 activations).
GAL-ASK: G3 (top ask). His prediction: smoother -> NTK survives -> leaks more. Observed: the opposite cluster order.
CAVEATS: two-cluster, NOT a monotone smoothness law (selu clusters with the sharp kinks; hardswish, also kinked, does not);
sign flips within the smooth-only set; MNIST only, N=2, n=13 activations - exploratory. Flowers32 free-c band pending
(a flowers oracle->free-c flip precedent exists, so dataset-dependence is OPEN). Does not flip the oracle.

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: smoothness really does keep the network linear longer (greens hug 1, kinked drop at step one) — yet kinked leak most, so linearization fidelity is not what drives leakage. WHAT WE DID: feature-stability-vs-T, 13 activations, T in {1,2,5,10,20,50}, MNIST N=2 LoRA r=8 (job 390026, 65/65).
Shown: five representative lines (softplus, sigmoid, gelu; relu, leaky-relu).
WHY THIS FUNCTION: fs = cos(grad_theta f(theta_0;x), grad_theta f(theta_T;x)) (experiments/ntk_verification.py
compute_feature_stability) is the direct NTK-survival read: 1 means the feature map did not rotate, i.e. the
linearization at theta_0 still describes the fine-tuned network.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: at every T the smoothest (sigmoid/softplus) sustain the highest fidelity and the kinked
(relu/leaky-relu) the lowest - robust at the extremes, two-cluster in the middle. fs > 0.99 (the 'linear regime' line)
only briefly, and only for sigmoid/softplus.
GAL-ASK: G3 - his PREMISE (smooth -> NTK survives) is right. His CONCLUSION (-> leaks more) is not: pooled
Spearman(feature stability, control-margin leakage) ~ 0 (-0.06; on ssim_norm +0.08, n=426). Kinked activations have the
WORST linearization fidelity and LEAK THE MOST - the dissociation. Fidelity does not drive leakage.
CAVEATS: weight-change confound at fixed lr (C1 activations take larger steps); the metric-scoped statement is on the
control margin (on ssim the correlation is mildly positive, +0.08 to +0.28 across subsets). Toy MLP, small n.

kinked tends to give higher gate diversity and rank

the first-layer update: each neuron hands the attacker one gate-weighted mixture of the training images — the activation appears only inside the gate matrix M   (scalar head; K classes: G = M ⊙ (VᵀC))

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: one object explains slides 3-5 — the activation enters only through the gates; step sigma' stamps each image a distinct binary code (the left grid: distinct COLUMNS = full rank = informative; images are the columns of M), bounded sigma'' only lets codes drift (the right grid: columns blur = rank collapses, but linearization stays faithful). SAY FIRST (context Yoad flagged as missing): what the adapter stores of the data is, at the first layer, a weighted SUM of the training images; the weight of image i at neuron k is the gate sigma-prime of the pre-activation — how open that neuron is on that image. Everything on this slide is about that one matrix of gates. WHAT WE DID: wrote down the one object every experiment probes. For a one-hidden-layer net the first-layer weight
signal factors as Omega = G X^T with G = D_v M D_c: v_k is neuron-only, c_i is sample-only, and the gate
M_ki = sigma'(<w_k, x_i>) is the ONLY factor coupling neuron k and image i. Each neuron hands the attacker one weighted
mixture of the training images; the number of genuinely different mixtures is at most rank(M). The activation enters the
whole theory only through sigma' - through M.
WHY THIS FUNCTION — SCALAR-HEAD SCOPE (expert fix, top priority): rank(G) = rank(M) is a SCALAR-output fact. For a K-class head each v_k and c_i is a VECTOR and G_ki = M_ki (v_k^T c_i), i.e. G = M HADAMARD (V^T C) — rank(G) != rank(M) in general: the head and residual geometry create or destroy mixing directions independently of the gates, so K enters the DATA GRADIENT itself, not only optimization capacity. In the scalar case, rank(G) = rank(M) needs D_v and D_c full rank (dead neurons drop D_v; at a KKT point non-support
vectors have c_i = 0, so the recoverable count is the rank over the SUPPORT-VECTOR columns). rank(M) = N is necessary
(else a d(N - rank)-dim blind subspace IN THIS frozen-gate first-order channel — a local first-order wall under the stated model, NOT proof the full map is non-invertible: a rank-deficient Jacobian does not imply non-injectivity, cf. x -> x^3); the data-generated gate code supplies
sufficiency - if G were free, rank gives only the row space, not the images.

6.3 >> selu 3.4 > gelu 2.9 > mish 2.4 > silu 2.3 > softplus 1.7 > tanh 1.6 > sigmoid 1.2 - and this ordering matches the
independently measured LoRA leakage, including the selu surprise. Softplus-beta is a one-parameter dial: beta 0.5 -> 50
takes eff_rank 1.4 -> 5.3 and mean|sigma''| 0.13 -> 3.3, traversing smooth -> ReLU. Fidelity: dM ~ sigma'' dz, so bounded
sigma'' gives small continuous drift (smooth wins); ReLU is frozen within a region and jumps at every kink crossing.

~ sigma'' |delta|^2 and |delta| differs across activations). The Dirac point: relu/leaky have autograd mean|sigma''| = 0 yet
the maximal gate range - the information is in the range, not pointwise sigma''. Conditioning, not bare rank, is what we
report downstream (Parts 2-3). second lossy stage: gradients of real images are not arbitrary either
is F locally injective and well-conditioned on the image manifold?
nothing downstream is a free choice — this map names the object (slide 11, measured on 12–13), the validity gates fix the regime (appendix 35), pre-registration fixes the questions (slide 16)

slides.notes:
THE SPINE (say it here, once): from this slide on, nothing is a free choice. The measurement map names the ONLY honest object (its noise-whitened spectrum — slides 11-12); the theory's own validity conditions fix every training knob (convergence band for lr, FD-verified island for T, gates for K — appendix 29); and the questions were pre-registered before the data came (slide 16). Each experiment slide carries its one-line theory link at the bottom. WHAT WE DID: Wrote the whole experiment as one deterministic map. A latent z=(z_1..z_N) generates the private images x=g(z); LoRA training turns them into the released adapter (A_T,B_T)=:F(z). Privacy is then a single question about F: is it locally injective and well-conditioned on the image manifold M_X?
WHY THIS FUNCTION: F has TWO lossy stages, and both help the attacker. (1) Images are not arbitrary pixels: realistic images occupy a manifold of local dimension k << d (moving between them takes coordinated changes: pose, lighting, shape, texture). (2) Gradients of real images are not arbitrary either: M_G = {grad L(X): X realistic} is a thin subset of gradient space. So LoRA may destroy vast amounts of ARBITRARY gradient information while still separating points of M_G: the attacker needs a RESTRICTED inverse, not a full one.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: This is the framing every later slide uses. The Jacobian program (next two slides) differentiates F; the secret-swap test (Part 3) is the finite-difference version of the same question (D vs D' = two points z, z').
GAL-ASK: This grew out of your May question about more data / distributions (G2): the honest way to ask "does the adapter carry the images" is to ask about the conditioning of F on the data manifold, not about a capacity number.
CAVEATS: The earlier rank theorem (gate matrix G = sigma'(<w_k,x_i>), Omega = G X^T; images survive in separable form iff rank(G) >= N) is a MECHANISM statement, not an attack: the attacker neither knows G nor can hold it fixed, because G depends on the very images being sought. Read rho >= N as a necessary floor on the first-order signal, not the verdict. (identifiability_feasibility_revision.tex:41-53.)

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: a private direction counts only if it clears the training-noise floor — whiten J by Sigma_seed, count singular values above the eps-line; the two heads record the same 80 directions and differ only in the floor. WHAT WE DID: Put the training-randomness floor into the Jacobian. IDEA PROVENANCE (on the slide, say it openly): the J_SNR whitening, q_eff(eps), and the controlled-coordinate experiment design were sparked in an AI working session; the 3-way estimator, permutation nulls, adequacy gates, and all runs are ours. Rerun the same fine-tune S times with different seeds at a fixed secret, estimate Sigma_seed, and whiten: J_SNR = Sigma_seed^(-1/2) J. Its singular values are per-direction signal-to-noise ratios; q_eff(eps) = #{i : eps*sigma_i(J_SNR) > 1} counts the private directions that clear the floor at perturbation budget eps. The figure is the r=8 spectrum for both task heads (MNIST, N=10, k=8, Nk=80, S=320, eps=1 line = the noise floor).
WHY THIS FUNCTION: In detection language this is a Fisher-information / Neyman-Pearson object: q_eff counts the directions whose OPTIMAL-detector SNR clears the chosen eps-threshold — an attack-independent channel diagnostic (eps*sigma=1 is a chosen SNR level, NOT the chance/information boundary). The col(J) restriction makes it conservative (Schur), which is the honest sense of "lower bound" here — never phrase it as weakest-attacker performance. Implementation: the full Sigma_seed (dimY ~ 14k) is unmeasurable at feasible S; we estimate the noise ONLY inside col(J) (Sigma_J = Cov(Q^T (Y - Ybar)), r_J x r_J) and whiten there. Observing only col(J) uses less of Y, so its Fisher <= the full Fisher (Schur complement) => q_eff|col(J) is a conservative lower bound on the true q_eff.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: 10-class buries MORE directions under the floor than binary (36 vs 59 of 80 at r=8): CE injects more seed noise into col(J) (iso_ratio 0.683 vs 0.491). Both heads record ALL 80 directions noise-free (r_J = 80): the difference is entirely in the floor, which is the point of the slide.
GAL-ASK: This is the ruler the rest of the talk uses. Worlds: A is proven by the ruler (attack-independent); C is excluded by the disjoint-adapter control (prior-independent); only what survives both is a genuine World-B leak. Where do you want me to spend compute: proving A at scale (a scoped guarantee) or building the World-B decoder?
CAVEATS: (1) q_eff needs S >~ 4*Nk seeds (empirically eff_rank(Sigma_seed) >~ r_J) AND stability across {S, 2S}; the retracted "2x multi-class amplification" (q_eff 97) was S=64 undersampling of a 160-dim noise cloud stacked on an underfit binary arm. (2) Leakage is r_J and q_eff, NEVER eff_rank (entropy effective rank reads backwards: smooth activations concentrate the spectrum, eff_rank drops while true leakage hits max). (3) q_eff is coordinate-dependent under reparametrization a -> M a'; hard_rank and iso_ratio are invariant; report q_eff in a fixed natural metric. (4) Exact unrolled Jacobian has a meta-gradient-chaos wall (FD rel err 3.9e-8 at lr=0.6 -> 1.0 at lr=0.7); island is lr<=0.6, T<=1000; always FD-gate the actual J before quoting q_eff. (5) d^2=2KL and the recovery reading assume Gaussian seed noise + local linearity of J: q_eff certifies LOCAL identifiability, not global invertibility. RECOVERY READING NOT YET LICENSED: until the controlled-secret calibration runs (E1 in the experiment guide: known-by-construction coordinates, test whether recovery error crosses at eps*sigma_i ~ 1), q_eff is an SNR diagnostic, not a validated recovery predictor — E1 is named on the decisions slide.

So "having enough dimensions" does not mean they point in useful directions; the d*rho >= N*k inequality sizes the NULL SPACE, not a capacity law. The rank-r LoRA manifold has dimension r(m+d-r), which is why a rank-count can be large while the spectrum is terrible.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: The figure is the concrete example that "rank-r LoRA => r images" is FALSE. The iso mechanism (seed-noise coupling into col(J)) explains the reversal at r=8 (10-class iso 0.683 > binary 0.491) but DECOUPLES at r>=N: at r=16 the iso gap flips (0.389 vs 0.808) yet q_eff still reverses (47 < 60). each dot = one trained adapter  ΔW = BA
the unit, not the whole program — the arms re-run it across swap targets, copy counts, class balance, context and similarity; removal, whole-composition and Jacobian variants flank it

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: one number per swap — d^2 is how far replacing one image moves the adapter, in units of seed noise; K seeds per side give the two clouds, and this unit runs under every arm. WHAT WE DID: The secret-swap test. Take a dataset D of N images; build D' by replacing ONE image (the target) with another. Fine-tune a LoRA on each K=50 times with different training seeds (headline K; K=20 for scouting). Each trained adapter is one point in flattened dW = BA space. D gives a cloud with mean mu(D) and seed-covariance Sigma; D' gives another. The whitened sensitivity d^2 = (mu(D') - mu(D))^T Sigma^-1 (mu(D') - mu(D)) is the swap's mean effect measured in units of the training noise.
WHY ONE IMAGE (if asked): a one-record change IS the neighbouring-datasets definition from DP / membership inference — the per-image privacy unit; it is the finest question the estimator can ask, and every composition effect is then measured by varying what surrounds that unit. And it is NOT the only design: the H gate and arm F use REMOVAL (leave-one-out, no swap), the atlas contrasts WHOLE compositions, and the Jacobian program perturbs all Nk latent directions at once — the swap is the discrete unit those all connect to. WHY THIS FUNCTION: This is the finite-difference version of the Jacobian question: J_SNR is the derivative of the same map, d^2 is the same object for a discrete data change (q_eff is literally the thresholded spectrum of this object, so the two programs are one). The noise covariance Sigma_seed IS the natural (Fisher) metric of the adapter space. Everything is computed in the dW = BA gauge, never on the raw A, B factors (BA = (BR)(R^-1 A): the factors are gauge-dependent, the product is not).
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: The same estimator runs on every arm of the battery (B dilution, C imbalance, D context, E duplication, S1 similarity, ViT LoRA, H gate); arms differ only in which image is swapped and what the surrounding dataset is.
GAL-ASK: This is the centrepiece: a leakage CEILING that does not depend on any attack, so we can test dataset-composition hypotheses without first building a decoder.
CAVEATS: The plug-in d-hat^2 is biased upward (Hotelling-T^2, ~dim/(K-dim)), so the reported statistic is NEVER the raw value: report against a sign-flip permutation null on the K paired diffs (v_j -> s_j v_j, s_j in {+1,-1}), which carries the identical estimator bias (same K, p, folds, shrinkage; only the labels flipped). sensitivity = d-hat^2_obs - mean(d-hat^2_null); p = fraction of null draws >= observed (floor 1/501 at 500 permutations). p is the PRIMARY readout while the magnitude estimator is unconverged — but keep the distinction: the permutation p answers a repeated-runs ESTIMATION question (K reseeds); a real attacker sees ONE adapter, and one-release severity is the population d (AUC = Phi(d/sqrt 2)). All p = 0.002 sit at the 500-permutation floor and cannot rank effects. Call magnitudes "resolved sensitivity at K" (d-hat^2_{K,p}), not lower bounds (next two slides).

runs.text: this bounds the change in adapter space, not pixel error —
to reach pixels, Δμ still has to go through the data→adapter Jacobian
one number for how hard the two datasets are to tell apart from a single release:
= 2·KL, so the KL divergence between the two adapter laws is
what a value of d means for the best possible attacker:
d = 1  →  AUC 0.76, best error 31%      d = 2  →  AUC 0.92, error 16%
⇒  a ceiling on detecting the change —
same seed-noise covariance as on slide 12: there it whitened the Jacobian direction by direction, here it whitens one mean shift
standard methods used here: Mahalanobis distance; the Neyman–Pearson optimal detector under equal-covariance Gaussians; Fisher information / Cramér–Rao

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: d^2 is a ceiling on ANY attacker's ability to notice the change — under equal-Sigma Gaussian it IS the optimal detector's SNR^2 (= 2KL = Fisher); it bounds the adapter shift, not pixels. WHAT WE DID: Chose the whitened (Mahalanobis) sensitivity d^2 as the ONE metric of the program and justified it by what it is equal to. Under the Gaussian, equal-covariance approximation the same number is simultaneously (1) the optimal-detector (Neyman-Pearson) SNR^2, the best ANY attacker can do at telling D from D'; (2) 2*KL(P_D' || P_D) between the with/without-change adapter distributions; (3) the Fisher information for the SCALAR shift t along delta-mu (Var(t-hat) >= 1/d^2 — for private coordinates the object is F_z = J^T Sigma^-1 J); (4) the Gaussian testing tradeoff for THIS neighbouring pair (not an f-DP guarantee — that needs all pairs). And it subsumes q_eff: q_eff is the thresholded spectrum of this object, so the discrete-dataset case is continuous with all the Jacobian work.
WHY THIS FUNCTION: The cartoon is why the raw norm ||delta-mu|| is the wrong ruler: the seed cloud is very anisotropic, so a swap that moves the adapter a small Euclidean distance along a QUIET direction is highly detectable, while a large move along the noisy long axis is invisible. Whitening measures every direction in its own noise units. Corollary: the whitening subspace must be SIGNAL-defined (top-p directions of the paired diffs), never Sigma's own top directions (those are exactly the noisy ones we should discount).
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: d^2 is an UPPER BOUND / NECESSARY CONDITION on every downstream attack, reconstruction included: if d^2 ~ 0 (the change is indistinguishable from reseeding) no attack can recover the change; if d^2 is large, recovery is PERMITTED, not achieved. That is exactly the posture we want for composition hypotheses: test the ceiling first, build decoders second.
ONE-RELEASE MEANING (say if asked what d means for a single released adapter): with equal priors the Bayes error is Phi(-d/2) and the AUC is Phi(d/sqrt(2)) — severity lives in the population d, not in the permutation p. CRB WORDING: d^2 is the Fisher information for the scalar shift t along Delta-mu (Var(t-hat) >= 1/d^2); for actual private coordinates the object is F_z = J^T Sigma^-1 J — never say "CRB for estimating Delta-mu". And d gives the testing tradeoff for THIS neighbouring pair only — not an f-DP guarantee (that needs all pairs). GAL-ASK: This is the "ceiling, not the attack" framing you asked me to keep honest in May. The all-attacker ceiling is the mutual-information / Fano rate-distortion bound; a prior-equipped (biased) attacker, e.g. the Direction-3 diffusion/SDS prior, can beat the Cramer-Rao floor but not Fano.
CAVEATS: (1) The four equivalences hold ONLY under equal-Sigma Gaussian. If Sigma(D) != Sigma(D') the optimal detector is quadratic (QDA) and pure Mahalanobis drops the covariance term: test Sigma-invariance first (eff_rank/spectrum of Sigma(D) vs Sigma(D')); if they differ, use symmetrized (Jeffreys) KL with the pooled Sigma. (2) The seed noise here is non-Gaussian (heavy tails, skew -2.3 / excess kurtosis 36 at N=4; NaN draws) so the skew/kurtosis diagnostic is a REQUIRED gate; if it fails, d^2 is a heuristic SNR, not "the optimal detector". The permutation null is robust to BOTH failures, which is why it is the primary readout. (3) d^2 bounds adapter-space error, NOT pixel MSE directly (the ssim-overclaim trap): recovering the image needs delta-mu pushed through the nonlinear data->adapter Jacobian; the composed Fisher bridge F_img = J^T Sigma^-1 J is scheduled, not built.

the binary cross-entropy loss on image xᵢ with its label
the gradient of that loss with respect to W₀
the Frobenius norm — the size of that gradient matrix
means the image exerts a large first-layer training force at the public model.

the first-layer update is Ω = Σᵢ gᵢxᵢᵀ: each image enters the weights through its own coefficient gᵢ. If the trajectory records those per-image gradients, the images that push hardest at the start should leave the largest trace — and
is a proxy for the magnitude of that per-image contribution at the public model.
the rival picture — the max-margin endpoint (KKT)
1 · train to convergence on data the model can separate;
2 · gradient descent then drifts to the max-margin solution;
3 · there the weights are built only from the support vectors — the images sitting exactly at margin 1, each with a dual weight λᵢ > 0. Everything further in contributes nothing.
so the two disagree about who is at risk:
everyone, in proportion to how badly the model fits them — or only the few images on the margin.
theory link: if the recording view is right, the base gradient must rank the trace sizes — this is its direct test
standard methods used here: the implicit-bias (max-margin) view of gradient descent on separable data, and its KKT conditions

CLAIM+HOW (the g0 claim): g0 at the PUBLIC model — one backward pass per image, no adapter access — already ranks which images leave larger adapter traces: rho=+0.78 at n=24; larger point estimate than the KKT dual (paired comparison pending); strong at low g0, saturating above (the terciles). WHAT WE DID: margin / support-vector test. For each target image compute g0 = Frobenius norm of the BCE gradient w.r.t. the FULL layer-0 weight at the PUBLIC base model theta_0 (margin_vs_sensitivity.py:75-91, one backward per image), then correlate with the per-image whitened sensitivity. Compared against the max-margin dual proxy lambda = sigmoid(-margin_T) and the raw base margin.
WHY THIS FUNCTION: read Omega = sum_i g_i x_i^T — image i enters the update with coefficient g_i; its public-model norm is the attacker-side predictor that needs NO adapter access.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: rho(sens, g0) = +0.857 at n=12 (job 260171, PASS vs the pre-registered +-0.15) and +0.777 at n=24 (job 272504; permutation p = 1e-4; 95% CI [0.53, 0.91]; graded INDETERMINATE by pre-registration — PRECISION reading (expert fix): the 0.15 was a CI-HALF-WIDTH precision target, not an effect-size band around zero; at n=24 the half-width is ~0.19 > 0.15, while the CI [0.53, 0.91] is nowhere near zero. Present the CI + the precision criterion, never a shaded zone around 0). Tercile structure (sorted ascending in g0): +0.88 low-g0, +0.50 mid, -0.12 high-g0 — the predictor is strong where the base model does little work and SATURATES once g0 is large (the sign-flip that kept it below PASS; WHY it saturates is open — one hypothesis: g_i carries the loss residual, which decays as fast-fit images are fit). GAL-ASK: G1 (direct inversion) reframed — the adapter is a gradient recording; whether it sits at a KKT point is testable (beta(T) diagnostic, slide R1) and currently says no.

runs.text: what full fine-tuning would write, and what the adapter is able to write
H is the gradient full fine-tuning would apply to the weights; η is the step size.

the adapter cannot write H. It writes only what the column space of B and the row space of A can represent: a component of H outside both is removed at first order, and what survives is scaled and recombined rather than orthogonally projected.
so the adapter is a filtered copy of the full gradient. Two questions follow:
does it keep the same images — and does it keep as much of each?
theory link: this is the one-step tangent picture; the released adapter is the whole T-step trajectory, and the measured object is J = ∂Y/∂a

slides.notes:
WHAT WE DID: state, before any measurement, what a single LoRA step is able to write into the weights compared with
what full fine-tuning would write. If H is the gradient full fine-tuning would apply and eta the step size, the adapter
cannot write H: it writes only the part of H that its factors can express - P_LoRA(H) = B B^T H + H A^T A.
WHY THIS FUNCTION: this is the one-step tangent picture, and it is the mechanism behind both of the questions that follow -
does the adapter keep the same images, and does it keep as much of each? It also explains why the seed shows up in the raw
factors: at this repo's init (A0 = 0, B0 random) the first step exposes the data only through the row space of a random B0.
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: P_LoRA is a self-adjoint PSD operator, NOT a projection (P^2 != P) - say that, because "LoRA projects
the gradient" is the natural but wrong shorthand. The released adapter is the whole T-step trajectory, not one step, which
is why the measured object is the end-to-end Jacobian J = dY/da rather than this formula.
CAVEATS: one-step statement; the T-step object is what we actually measure; the init convention matters (A0 = 0 here, the
Hugging Face default is B0 = 0, which puts the exact structure on the other side).

left: adapters compared by their merged update ΔW = BA.   right: the same adapters compared by their raw pair (B, A).
two adapters are compared by their updates themselves — how far ΔW₁ sits from ΔW₂ as matrices. Nothing about the recipe, the seed or the labels enters.
ΔW is the object that is actually released and used, and it does not care how the update was split into B and A — two adapters that act identically sit at distance zero.
cluster on that distance matrix alone; the picture is a 2-D embedding of the same distances, so groups that look separated really are.

standard methods used here: t-SNE for the two-dimensional picture; the adjusted Rand index (Hubert–Arabie) for the score

CLAIM+HOW: WHICH data is readable from Delta W and only the seed from the raw factors — 169-adapter atlas clusters by composition (ARI 1.0) vs by seed; the cross-fitted effect size over the recipe baseline is under re-audit — lead with ARI. WHY THIS FUNCTION: LoRA has the exact gauge symmetry BA = (BR)(R^-1 A) — only Delta W is gauge-invariant; the raw factors carry the init seed (P_LoRA at B=0 exposes H A^T A, the row space of a random A). The atlas is the empirical gauge-contrast: seed visible in (B, A), scrubbed in Delta W.

•  SimuDy reframe — agreed on your side?

slides.notes:
WHAT WE DID: placed every experiment in the three-worlds map (thesis_note_v2 section 4) and listed the four decisions I need.
THE DISCIPLINE IN ONE LINE (thesis_note_v2 section 4): World A is proven by the ruler (attack-independent); World C is excluded by the disjoint-adapter control (prior-independent); only what survives both is a genuine World-B leak. A is a SCOPED guarantee — no local, per-image, linearised information survives under Gaussian seed noise; it is not a guarantee against priors, higher-order effects, or the composition channel (E6 is exactly such an escape).
E7 — THE OPEN MILESTONE (World B): robust adapter-only inversion, minimise ||Y - F(theta_0, x_hat)|| over candidate images. Four controls keep it honest: (i) disjoint-adapter subtraction (leakage above the prior — excludes World C); (ii) staged Jacobians across activations (the activation crux carried through to reconstruction); (iii) local-vs-global init (optimisation failure != non-identifiability); (iv) render the weakest / strongest singular directions as image edits. Full-gradient reconstruction works (SSIM up to ~0.99 MNIST/CIFAR/Flowers; ViT faces 0.38/0.26/0.52); the bridge decoder reaches 0.930 cosine converged (0.951 was best-epoch — quote the converged number); direct inversion recovers N=4 and superposes at N=10; q_eff(eps) shows the directions are present — 51/117/150/156 at eps=0.3/1/3/10 in the NORMALIZED LOCAL coordinates (S=640->1280 stable, adequacy gates pass); the CURVE is the object, not the max, the count is coordinate-dependent, and which directions count as "private" (random pixels vs manifold tangents) is part of the threat model — an extraction gap, not a missing-information gap — STRONGLY SUGGESTIVE, not proven — and never argue across cells: a high q_eff in adapter Y_A plus a failed pixel attack on adapter Y_B does NOT show Y_B is extraction-limited (Y_B's image directions may genuinely be absent); the evidence mixes N/datasets/activations; the clean World-B test is ONE fixed cell with q_eff(eps) + near-truth init + random init + disjoint-adapter baseline together (that is the E7 opener).
DECISIONS: (1) SimuDy reframe (async pointer 2026-06-29) — direct weight inversion overlaps SimuDy; we reframed DI as the known-recipe upper bound; is that settled on your side? (2) Scale: keep to toy + theory (where the ruler is exact) or push to ViT / Stable Diffusion LoRA (where the ruler is only estimable)? (3) F5 shared-perturbation (cross-dataset) compute: honest null at n=8, the rotation variant is suggestive — worth the GPU budget? (4) Instance-level atlas zoo (same digits, different exemplars) — the honest open item after the content-level +0.989; build it?

runs.text: the first-layer signal is gates × data; a rank-deficient gate leaves a blind subspace
–  M is the gate: how open neuron k's valve is on image i
–  the activation enters only through σ′ — only through M
–  necessary, not sufficient: with G free, only the row space is fixed
–  at a KKT point non-support vectors have
scope: scalar-output head.  For a K-class head, G = M ⊙ (VᵀC) and rank(G) ≠ rank(M) in general — the head and residual geometry mix independently of the gates.

slides.notes:
SCALAR-HEAD SCOPE (expert fix): everything on this slide is the SCALAR-output case. K-class: G = M HADAMARD (V^T C); rank(G) != rank(M) in general. Also: the blind subspace is a LOCAL first-order wall in the frozen-gate channel under the stated model, not a proof of non-invertibility of the true map (rank-deficient Jacobian does not imply non-injective; x -> x^3). SCOPE: Theorem (identifiability_rank_bound.tex, thm:main): assume (H1) Omega = G X^T, (H2) G FIXED and known (the frozen-known-G reading), (H3) v_k, c_i != 0. If rank(M) = k < N then Phi^{-1}(Omega) = X + K with every row of H in ker G, dim K = d (N - k) >= d >= 1: a continuum of datasets fits, and the N! permutation symmetry cannot fill it. This is a NECESSARY condition for recovery (rank(M) = N), not a sufficient one: if G were free, rank gives only the row space (any remix (G R^-1)(R X^T) matches Omega). What breaks the ambiguity is that G is GENERATED by the data through sigma'(<w_k, x_i>) at known theta_0 — combinatorially rigid for kinked activations (discrete gate codes), soft for smooth ones (thesis_note_v2 section 1).
SUPPORT-VECTOR CAVEAT: rank(G) = rank(M) needs D_v, D_c full rank. At a KKT point non-support vectors have c_i = 0 so D_c drops rank, and dead neurons drop D_v — the recoverable count is the rank over the support-vector columns.
LORA: a rank-r adapter replaces Omega by a rank-r observation, tightening the ceiling to min(rank(M), r, N) (tex lines 253-259). A rank-r update is NOT 'r numbers' (the rank-r manifold has dimension r(m+d-r)) — the ceiling counts separable samples, not bits.
PROVENANCE: notes/identifiability_rank_bound.tex lines 95-118 (observation), 159-183 (theorem + proof), 253-259 (LoRA ceiling); notes/linearization_leakage_theory.tex 72-87.

runs.text: four names for one number, and the six rules every reported value obeys
(equal-Σ Gaussian; Δμ = mean adapter shift under the swap, Σ = seed-noise covariance)
primary = detection: the sign-flip permutation p (500-permutation resolution floor — p cannot rank effect sizes)
coarsened, not an independent metric; the H-gate memorisation score is the only cross-metric check
magnitude = resolved sensitivity at the stated K (population subspace restriction is conservative; the finite-K estimator is not treated as converged); comparisons only at fixed K
K ≥ 50 headline; {K, 2K} adequacy gate; shrinkage floor; Σ-invariance + Gaussianity gates reported
everything in the ΔW = BA gauge, never raw A / B factors
no 'privacy leakage' framing for any magnitude until the H gate closes — 'sensitivity' until then
for the scalar displacement t along Δμ — not a pixel-MSE bound; pixels only via the data-latent Jacobian

slides.notes:
THE FOUR EQUIVALENCES (whitened_sensitivity_metric.md lines 49-70): under the Gaussian equal-Sigma approximation d^2 is simultaneously (1) the optimal-detector (Neyman-Pearson) SNR^2 — the best any attacker can do at telling D from D'; (2) 2 KL(P_1 || P_0) between the with/without-change adapter distributions; (3) the Fisher information for the SCALAR shift t along Delta-mu (Var(t-hat) >= 1/d^2 — for private coordinates the object is F_z = J^T Sigma^-1 J; never phrase as "CRB for estimating Delta mu") — NOT pixel MSE (recovering the image pushes Delta mu through the nonlinear data-latent Jacobian of the training map; never state it as a direct reconstruction-MSE bound — the ssim-overclaim class); (4) the Gaussian testing tradeoff for THIS neighbouring pair — not an f-DP guarantee for the algorithm (that requires all neighbouring pairs). One-release meaning: Bayes error Phi(-d/2), AUC Phi(d/sqrt 2). It subsumes q_eff: q_eff is the thresholded spectrum of this object.
WHEN THE EQUIVALENCES FAIL: (S1) if Sigma(D) != Sigma(D') the optimal detector is quadratic (QDA) and pure Mahalanobis drops the KL covariance term — test Sigma-invariance first; if they differ, use symmetrised (Jeffreys) KL with the pooled Sigma. (S2) seed noise is non-Gaussian (heavy tails, NaN draws) — the skew/kurtosis diagnostic is a required gate; if it fails d^2 is a heuristic SNR, not 'the optimal detector'. The permutation null is robust to BOTH failures, which is why it is the primary readout (rule 1).
ESTIMATOR: 3-way disjoint cross-fit (fold A -> subspace U, fold B -> Delta mu . U, fold C -> lambda), rotated and averaged; consistent with unbiased (reads zero on signal-free data at every K) (null-diag job 212413: reseed-vs-reseed ~0 at every K while real swaps read 8 (K=50) -> 22 (K=100) at p = 0.002); K-drift +6.3% (3-way) vs +44% (old 2-way).

runs.text: the sensitivity number is built from K training runs — reuse those runs twice and it measures its own noise
how much the number moves when the seed count doubles — an honest number should barely move

d̂² needs two things from the same K runs: which direction the swap moved the adapter, and how big the seed noise is along that direction. Take both from one pool and the noise floor is measured along a direction its own samples helped pick — it comes out too small, so the number comes out too big.
an honest number should not care how many seeds you give it. Run at K, then at 2K, over 60 synthetic datasets: if it drifts, it is still measuring itself. Gate: under 15%.
three disjoint seed folds, rotated: one picks the direction, one measures the shift, one measures the noise. Drift falls from +44% (retracted) to +6.3%.
the swap read, minus what the same estimator reads when the labels are shuffled
no-signal data reads zero at every K; a real one-image swap reads p = 0.002.
and what it still is not
the absolute value still grows with K. So magnitudes are quoted at a stated K, and the p-value is the headline.
this is the licence for part 4: every magnitude in the arms is quoted from the three-way estimator, at a stated K, with the sign-flip p as the headline
standard methods used here: cross-fitting / sample splitting in the double-machine-learning style; the sign-flip permutation test

slides.notes:
CLAIM+HOW: the estimator is null-calibrated — 3-way disjoint folds cut the K-doubling drift from +44% to +6%, no-signal data reads zero, and the sign-flip null carries the identical bias (magnitude still moves with K: stable ordering, not convergence). TRANSITION (Yoad: explain the move to the data experiments): the point of this slide is the LICENSE — once the estimator reads zero on nothing and loud on one image, the same single number can be asked about dataset composition; every part-4 arm is one such question with a pre-registered prediction (next slide). The arm-B bars formerly shown here live on slide 16 panel B (K=100). WHAT WE DID: Found and fixed a self-deception in the estimator, then checked the fixed one reads zero on signal-free data at every K (consistent with unbiased). The first cross-fit was 2-WAY: the subspace U and the noise floor lambda came from one seed fold, only the numerator delta-mu from a disjoint fold. But lambda was then measured along a subspace its OWN samples helped define: selection-biased small (winner's curse), so d-hat^2 INFLATED with K instead of converging. Arm-B post-mortem: d^2(N=64) went 63 -> 161 as K went 50 -> 100 — a pure estimator bug, since fixed (do not present it as a scientific claim that was withdrawn). Fix: a 3-WAY disjoint split, rotated over all ordered fold-triples (double-ML style): fold A -> U (top-p right singular vectors of fold-A paired diffs), fold B -> numerator (delta-mu_B . u_i)^2, fold C -> denominator lambda_i (variance of fold-C reseed adapters along u_i).
WHY THIS FUNCTION: Left panel: over 60 synthetic datasets, the population-mean drift of E[d^2] from K to 2K is +44% for the 2-way estimator vs +6.3% for the 3-way (gate <= 15%); self-test 4/4 PASS (orthogonal -> detect, aligned -> mask, null -> flat, K-convergence). Right panel (null-diag, job 212413): the 3-way statistic on NO-SIGNAL data (reseed-vs-reseed, K=200) reads -0.001 at N=4 and +0.003 at N=16 with p = 0.58 / 0.42 and q_eff = 0, i.e. zero reads zero at every K; a real one-image swap at the same recipe reads 22 / 24 / 24 / 13 at N = 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 with p = 0.002 (arm B reconfirm, job 130198 — the K=100 read; panel labelled).
WHY REPRESENTATIVE: A third calibration on real data: the S1 similarity ladder's d=0 identity rung (swap the target for itself) reads sens = 0, p = 1.000 exactly (job 268959). Shrinkage rho for the whitening is chosen by CV against the null (the rho maximizing d-hat^2_obs - mean d-hat^2_null); small-eigenvalue floor mandatory.
GAL-ASK: This is the rigor you asked for in May (G2, "not best runs"): every reported number now comes with a null, a p-value and a K-convergence check, and the retractions are listed openly (appendix A4).
CAVEATS: The 3-way fix lowered the absolute scale but real-data d^2 still grows with K (arm B N=4: 8 -> 22 as K 50 -> 100, ~2.6x per doubling; k2k gives 46 at K=200 — while the reseed-vs-reseed null stays ~0 at K = 50/100/200, job 212413; denominator flat). The absolute d^2 is a fixed-K relative statistic + p-value, NOT a converged point estimate; what is solid is p = 0.002 at every N and the N-shape (flat, decline at N=32) being identical at K=50 and K=100. Because the null stays at ~0 and flat, the growth reads as signal-direction RESOLUTION — but this does NOT prove the finite-K estimator sits monotonically below the population value (only the population-level subspace restriction is provably conservative; the adaptive finite-K estimator can fluctuate either way). Call it "resolved sensitivity at K" (d-hat^2_{K,p}); quote and compare only at fixed K and fixed p; the detection p-value is the headline. Single-draw K-flatness is a knife-edge, hence the gate is a population mean over datasets, not one run.

CONSTRUCTION (jacobian_spectrum.py q_eff_colspace, lines 580-620): J = dY/da is the end-to-end Jacobian of the flattened adapter w.r.t. the Nk secret coefficients, exact by double backprop (checked vs finite differences to ~8 decimals). The energy-overlap metric was chance-baseline-confounded and the full Sigma_seed is unmeasurable at feasible S, so estimate the noise ONLY where the signal lives: Q = orthonormal basis of col(J) (dim r_J <= Nk); project the S seed draws n_s = Q^T (Y_s - Ybar); Sigma_J = Cov(n_s) [r_J x r_J]; whiten inside col(J): F = (Q^T J)^T Sigma_J^-1 (Q^T J). Estimable at S >~ few * r_J, no shrinkage floor for unsampled directions (ridge 1e-12 x mean diagonal only). q_eff(eps) = #{i : eps sqrt(lambda_i(F)) > 1}. The full-space variant (snr_spectrum, lines 546-578) uses Woodbury: Sigma = rho I + M^T M / (S-1) so Sigma^-1 = rho^-1 [I - M^T (rho (S-1) I + M M^T)^-1 M]; only the S x S system is inverted.
ISOTROPY: iso = tr(Sigma_J) / (mu r_J) with mu the isotropic per-coordinate noise level: ~1 means the noise genuinely has variance in col(J); ~0 means the noise avoids the signal directions. A flat eig/mu profile = uniform attenuation; a split (some ~1, some ~0) = structured masking (e.g. A-block directions see attenuated B-block init noise).
INVARIANCE: hard_rank and iso_ratio are basis-free; eff_rank (entropy of sigma(J)) reads spectral SHAPE, not leakage, and moves backwards as CE / smooth activations flatten the tail (LESSONS_LEARNED.md 78); q_eff depends on the METRIC / PARAMETERIZATION of the private coordinates and on eps (rotating the observation basis of col(J) changes nothing — the eigenvalues of J^T Sigma^-1 J are invariant; reparameterizing the SECRETS does) — report as a lower-bound count '>= X at K', adequacy-gated ({K,2K} stability and eff_rank(Sigma) >~ p). Honesty gates: S >~ 4 r_J (the retracted '97 directions' used S=64 << r_J=160); q_eff stable from S to 2S.
